source_title: Prehistoric America vol. 2: Emblematic mounds and animal effigies
author: Stephen D. Peet

where.page_or_leaf: Fig. 167, p.259, leaf n298

caption_or_quote: "Fig. 167.-Group at Merrill's Springs." Text p.260: "In the group at Merrill's springs, the wild goose appears and with it the eagle, and just at the springs two buffalo and an eagle effigy and a row of round mounds. See Fig. 167."
shows: Group plan along the Lake Mendota shore: Merrill's spring, ploughed field, low ground, effigies (goose/eagle, 'buffalo'), linears with lengths 200/300 ft, a row of round mounds
licence_basis: Published 1890 (before 1931) - public domain in the US
notes: Viewed at 800 px. Wisconsin Archeologist (o.s. 20, 1921) says the Black Hawk Country Club tract at Mendota Heights 'near Merrill Springs' preserves 'three bear effigies, two linear and three conical mounds and the widely known goose effigy'. Peet's figure shows the springs group including a goose-like bird; whether it extends ~800 m S to the club point (43.0797,-89.4608; PLSS Sec. 17 T7N R9E) is not proven - schematic, no scale bar beyond foot labels. A. B. Stout's accurate 1905 plat of the 12-mound club group is cited only in 1940s volumes (not PD by our rule) and was not found in a pre-1931 issue.
